newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-ECUADOR SPRING SHOCK ON CHILAVERT OFF-DAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ECUADOR SPRING SHOCK ON CHILAVERT OFF-DAY.

text.p: Ecuador sprang the first shock of the Copa America on Saturday as Paraguay's Jose Luis Chilavert, the self-proclaimed best goalkeeper in the world, suffered an off-day.
The unfancied Ecuadoreans beat Paraguay, South America's on-form team and one of the few to bring their top players to the tournament, 2-0 in group A.
In the day's other match, Argentina scored their first goal of the tournament after 175 minutes of trying play before finally overcoming Chile 2-0.
Chilavert, who regularly scores goals from free kicks and penalties, was on the wrong end when Wellington Sanchez scored for Paraguay in the 72nd minute direct from a free kick.
Ariel Graziani buried Paraguay when he scored with superbly struck shot with Chilavert rooted to his goal-line four minutes from the end.
"To score against Chilavert, the best goalkeeper in the world, excites anyone," said a delighted Graziani afterwards.
Unfortunately, the game excited few other people as the two teams produced yet another uninspired affair to follow the two dull opening encounters in the same group on Wednesday.
Players and coaches blamed the altitude of Cochabamba, 2,600 metres above sea level high.

"In this group, all the teams are very compact, nobody is giving anything to anyone and you have to be very imaginative and creative to break the stalemate," said Paraguay coach Paulo Cesar Carpegianni.

Argentina, who drew 0-0 with Ecuador in their first game, looked set to complete two games without hitting the target until Sergio Berti scored from what may have been an offside position in the 85th minute.

Shortly afterwards, Marcelo Gallardo added a second to take Argentina level on four points with Ecuador. Paraguay have three and Chile none but, with the top two in each group plus the two best third-placed teams all advancing to the quarter-finals, nobody had yet qualified or been eliminated.
The two games were featured on a double bill, which attracted only 8,000 fans.
It was yet another poor turnout in a tournament which has been devalued because it clashes with the region's World Cup qualifying matches, forcing most countries to rest their top players.
Brazil, with a full-strength squad, are hot favourites for the title, especially after they began by demolishing Costa Rica 5-0 on Friday in group C.
However, their camp was hit by rumours of discontent after tempestous striker Romario was surprisingly substituted 15 minutes from time.
Romario, who had just scored a spectacular goal and was clearing enjoying himself, was caught uttering Portuguese obsencities by a television close-up as he slunk off the pitch.
Coach Mario Zagallo, whose team face Mexico in their second group C game on Monday, denied there had been a rebellion.
"There is no problem, his behaviour has been good," Zagallo said following a training session.
"Being substituted is part of the game. I didn't like it when I was a player and it is natural he wasn't happy. The fact that he might have sworn is irrelevant."
Organisers in the city of Sucre, which is hosting group B matches, promised the stadium would be in full working order for the rest of the competition.

They said measures would be taken to make sure the electricity and phones work and that construction material, which was left dumped around the stadium when Peru played Uruguay on Thursday, would be cleared up.
